main_body: Brick-fronted stove body with a recessed firebox and a grey panel, under a dark slate hood. A brick chimney rises above the hood.
top_band: Hood cap at rows ~21-25, dark slate grey with a slightly lighter top edge. It reads as a sloped roof or awning on top of the front, not a horizontal surface of the stove. No lighter horizontal top surface sits above the main body's front face.
evidence: Reading the middle column from the top: the chimney (rows 8-20) is a flat brick face seen head-on. The hood (rows 21-26) is a dark slate trapezoid with only a faint lighter top row, and its tone is the same family as the panel below, so it is a hat on a front elevation. Below it sit a grey rail panel (rows 28-35) and a brick front with a firebox (rows 37-46). All three are vertical faces drawn straight on. The firebox frame is inset and there is a shadow under the hood, but nothing shows a horizontal surface of the stove itself seen from above. The stove top is hidden, and the hood is too thin and dark to count as a top surface.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark purple-brown that leans toward the neighbouring brick, which is fine. The firebox has good flame detail with 4-5 orange steps. The rest is thinner than the references. The slate hood and the grey panel are large areas of nearly flat colour with only 3-4 steps. The bricks are single flat tones separated by mortar lines, with no per-brick highlights or speckle. The chimney is a big flat brick field. Overall it looks flatter and more sticker-like than the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps and textured roofs and stones.
